evidence.quote: From {{inh|en|enm|slendre}}, {{m|enm|sclendre}}, from {{der|en|fro|esclendre||thin, slender}}, from {{der|en|dum|slinder||thin, lank}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*slindraz||sliding, slippery}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*h₃sleydʰ-||to slip}}. Cognate with {{cog|bar|Schlenderling||that which dangles}}, {{cog|de|schlendern||to saunter, stroll}}, {{cog|nl|slidderen}}, {{m|nl|slinderen||to wriggle, creep like a serpent}}, {{cog|nds|slindern||to slide on ice}}. More at {{l|en|slide}}, {{l|en|slither}}.

"thin, lean, not fat or fleshy," earlier sclendre (late 14c.), Anglo-French esclendre,… See origin and meaning of slender. from Old French esclendre "thin, slender," which could be from Old Dutch slinder , but according to OED the connection is doubtful.
